The closing scene OF this extraordinary drama,
exceeded in interest every other act of it, The Jury


went out about SIX at night, and remained out ten
hours. During that time large mob collected


around the City Hall, and knots and groups of per-


sons assembled all about the Park, discussing the
probable verdict and all the facts in the case Hour
after hour passed by, and the interest increased
All sorts OF rumors were afoat to the position OF


the Jurors, and the scenes in the Jury Room. The
officers listened at the key-hole and reported pro-
gres and it spread like wildfre through the crowd.
that the Jury stoed seven for MURDER three for man
slaughter, aud two for excusable homicide Then,
alter discussing it hour, they stood seven for MUIR

1t another hour and they stood ten to two and there

In the mean time, the Judge had returned, waited
till midnight, and then gone back home. Groups OF
anxious persons fingered about the Courtroom
The prisoner, tired, and worn out, gave way to
the impulses of nature, laid down on BENCH threw


handkerchief over his face, and slept soundly while
the Jury were deciding the fate of his existence.
The time-the p!ace-the circumstances-thes solemn
stiffness of the night, ALI combined to form scene
not easily forgotten


AT last, when the verdict was agreed upon-the
Judge was sent for and it was soon whispered about
that it was fatal The prisoner was awoke, and his
countenance fell. The Judge and Jury at last faced
each other for the last tmethe prisoner was told TO

or TWO burst into tears The prisoners heart almost
died within him. Morrill, then applied TO the Court
for time to present their exceptions, and the Court
agreed to meet this morning at ten o'clock, to hear
them Colt was then removed to prison.


Now comes, then, the most exciting part OF the
drama will he be hung-or will new trial be
granted Will the Governor dare to pardon him =!
We think not. The verdict seems to give general
satisfaction. The public have had their eye on Colt
rom the time of his arrest till this hour and had
he verdict not been MURDER" we don't know
what would have been the consequence. The pub
c have been cheated so often, that Colt has to sui

This extraordinary, and wearying, and exciting
trial has at length been brought to close The
Court was crowded all day and over hundred la
dies of all ages, and of all styles of beauty were
there. Col Edwards was the most happy looking
and unconcerned creature in the whole room. Many
distinguished lawyers and legislators were present;
and very, very lovely young girl sat at the right
end of the bench, but took part in the delibera

Mr. WHITING concluded his very able speech by
half past 2 He spoke in all SIX hours. The Jury
then went to dine at Baron's-so did the prisoner,
walking through the park as free as air-almost.-
AT four they all returned, when Judge Kent deli
vered his charge, which occupied hour and forty
two mntes, and which was dead against the pri-
sonsr. The Jury then retired few minutes, appa-
parently disposed to disagree.


IL O'CLOCK. Court kept open till this hour.

tea-room, and there refreshed themselves for less
than an hour They have just sent to the jury TO
know if they had agreed, or were likely to agree.
The jury sent word back that they had not agreed
they could not agree-and there was no possibility
of their agreeing. The Court then adjourned to 10
o'clock on Tuesday morning, leaving word with the
officers that if the jury should come to an agree
ment during the night, that the Court should be
for.

been out hours. No agreement yet.


ONE o'CLocK.-The jury have not yet agreed and
one or two Of the fat men getting very sleepy. A
good deal of angry discussion going on.


HALF PAST ONE o'cLocK. Still no verdict; the
jury who were tolerably noisy and argumentative
about and 8 o'clock, have now settled down into
tolerable calm; still looking angry and black at
each other.


Two o'cIocK.-No verdict One of the Jurors
asked for glass of water; two or three asleep and
snoring Monroe Edwards in his cell, dreaming Of
lands in Texas, and slaves in Martinique, but not

freshment allowed the fury except little tea and

STANFORD, Or. Dec 2, 1872
Society and Soirkes in Stamfrd-Eating Dancing,


Fyirting, and Phiiosophising.


DEAR BENNKTr--


Seeing frequently communications from the
country in your interesting paper, upon the subject
of local occurrences, it has occurred to me that it
would afford interest to your readers for you to have
a correspondent in this place. where gossip and per-
sonal SANDER pass more current than the bills of
the best bank in our country; and having but little
business to occupy my attention during the winter
months, Propose giving you an occasional sketch
OF what going amongst us, with the privilege of
a corner in the Herald.


There have been many occurrences of late upon
which gOod" margins might have beea composed,
had any one taken the trouble to correspond with
you; but let pass over all old affairs, and take
review OF the splendid soirte which came off at the
principal hotel, kept by Mr.. Seely, last evening.


Soon after the sun had sunk beneath the western
hills" carriages were running in every direction
through our streets, collecting the ladies, and about
9 O'Clock the ball room wasthrown open and short
ly It was crowded with The Young and the gay Of
both sexes, and probably more social company
never convened together upon any former occasion
in old Stamford II composed of all classes
and all seemed tofeel free and equal spirit predo-
mlnant within them, The ladies were really beau
utul, and it afforded some amusement to hear the
gentlemen, grouped by themselves in end of the
room, discussing the peculiar charms of this lady
and that lady. II was affirmed by seemingly love-
stricken youth that the younger Miss ~ was per
feet angel, and would be the queen of the dance
that evening. Another thought her sister looked
more graceful, and others expressed themselves
partial to the beautiful and accomplished Misses IT,
while others thought Miss F., Miss Y, or Miss G
would compare with any lady in the room. Your
correspondent took impartial survey of the dear
ere atures, Tor he considered them all handsome,
graceful, and accomplished.


The ladies' being thoroughly criticized, the gen
tlemen took their partners for the first cotlop and
after several had been danced, the company were
refreshed with ice cream, and other e cetsras TIE
dancing then renewed. and continued without
lntermislon till supper was announced, when the
gentlemen escorted the ladies into an adjoining
room, where table was SET with all the good
things of this life. We shall not stop TO mention
how the ladies looked when they ate, or how they
pouted when this thing or that thing was passed to
them. 1t is enough to say that they all seemed to
have good appettes, and they enjoyed the supper
very well. Dancing was again commenced, and
kept up till about one O'clock, when the company
adjourned well pleased with the entertainment OF the
evening.


might have taken more notes had anticipated
giving you history Of the ball, but shall be more
particular at the next, which will take place In Two
weeks. There are other topics upon which might
extend my remarks, but will leave them till ano-
Their occasion, and till see whether you deem this
worthy place in your paper, Gum NUNc.
